volume.author: spec-author seat, group G5 Owner surface, round 1

contents.entry: Mechanism: the bridge, the provider, the dark flag
Provider choice: self-hosted ntfy on the cluster
Push delivery: ntfy config, the phone's path, egress, privacy, receipts, go-live proof
How it starts without an agent typing
Every wait, its timeout and its fallback
State paths and their cleanup scripts

pointers.sibling: JSON schema of push.receipt, push.failed and push.skipped
System lane card builder: the card record
Go inbox: this node ships dark until the inbox is live
Tailnet front door: the link the push carries opens through it
Alerts screen: owner-acts alerts may also push
Lease service: one sender at a time
pointers.shared: The outside probe publishes on its own topic of the same ntfy server
Where this node goes live in the one cut-over order of the book

purpose.is: The bridge tells the owner's phone that a card is waiting (and, by config, that an owner-acts alert fired) with a short push that opens the bearings page, and records a receipt per card so the system knows the phone was told.
purpose.is-not: It is not a second surface: the push carries no decision and takes no answer; the page is where he decides. It never carries the key.
purpose.why: Cards sat on a page the owner could not see while he was away from the desk (C32, 40 minutes; the 2026-10-14 ~03:55Z phone message about bureaucracy); the ruling on C58 added a phone push channel bridged after the Go inbox with acks.
purpose.decisions: C58 comms (phone push after the inbox), D20 one surface (the push is a doorbell, not mail: V13), D23 pods with no secret access (the provider token lives on the host), build-mode rule (ships dark, goes live by its own ticket).

field.name: card, tier, about, decide, rec, options, deadline

record.field: from N-28; only tier stable pushes by default (config phone_push.tiers)
card.unwatched, watcher.dead, page.down 500 on stable, front-door.failed, push.stalled, line.halted: the states in which the page itself may not be able to tell him

input.text: The card is the traversal's start. Alerts are a second, configurable input because they are exactly the cases where the page cannot carry the news; the list is phone_push.alert_kinds in the service config, reviewed as a pull request.

record.field: the card id (or the alert record id)
sha256 of the topic name, so the record proves which topic without naming it
after 3 attempts; an alert on N-41; the card is unaffected

dark (phone_push.enabled false), tier not pushed, done (card closed before the send), seen (card.shown on its tier), quiet-hours (config, owner-set; not terminal, step 7 re-evaluates), duplicate, or shadow (not the lease holder)

the owner opened the push's click URL (N-32 sees the receipt id in the URL fragment and writes it through the bridge) or the page drew the card after the receipt (card.shown); the evidence that the push reached a person, not only the provider

output.text: One receipt per card at most (operation key N-52/push.send/<card>/r1, shared/contracts.xml#operation-keys); a card that closes before the send is skipped; push.receipt says the provider accepted the message, push.observed says the owner saw it; delivery is at least once (#push-delivery).

mechanism.where: Go service (D01), package internal/owner/pushbridge inside coq.service; a subscriber (class tail) on N-31 with filter kinds card plus phone_push.alert_kinds and tiers phone_push.tiers.
mechanism.step: Hold the lease pushbridge from N-02 (ttl 15 s, renew every 5 s) so exactly one sender runs even if two service instances overlap during an upgrade; a non-holder subscribes and does nothing but count (shadow), ready to take the lease on expiry.

On a card record: check phone_push.enabled (dark flag), the tier, quiet hours, whether card.done already exists, and whether card.shown already exists for the card on its tier (the owner's page drew it, nodes/N-31/spec.xml#output); write push.skipped 100 with the reason (dark, tier, quiet-hours, done, seen, duplicate) when any says no; quiet-hours is the only reason step 7 revisits.

Compose the push (look section): title from about, body from decide with the recommended label, priority from the cause code (500 and 503 high, 422 and 423 default, 300 low), a click action to the tailnet page URL without the key (the phone holds the cookie from its first open; N-34 security), tags by kind. Run the comms checker (N-30's commscheck: sentences of 15 words or fewer, ticket ids with full titles, no key pattern, no em dash); a violation is a system defect written as push.refused 400 and an alert, and the push is not sent.

The send is an outbox effect (shared/contracts.xml#outbox): the intent row commits with the decision, the sender POSTs to the provider with the publish token of #push-delivery from ${COQ_STATE}/owner/push/token (mode 0600) and a 10 s timeout; retries 3 (10, 30, 90 s, the coqGate ladder's first three rungs, V05) on a network or 5xx error; a 4xx is not retried (a bad token or topic is a config defect) and is push.failed at once with the reason.

Store.Commit push.receipt 200 with operation key N-52/push.send/<card>/r1 and the provider's message id as the effect's external id (a replay returns the first receipt: the other instance sent it, stop). On failure after 3, push.failed 500.

On card.done within 60 s of the receipt (the owner answered quickly), nothing; the push is already delivered. No push is ever recalled or edited; the page is the truth. A click on the push or a card.shown after the receipt writes push.observed 200 once per card.

Scan, level-triggered every 60 s: list cards on pushed tiers that are still open and have no receipt, no failed record and no terminal skip older than 60 s, and send them; a card skipped only for quiet-hours is listed again when the quiet window ends and pushed then if it is still open and not seen, so quiet hours delay a push and never drop it.
mechanism.text: Why dark until the inbox is live: the owner's reply to a push is a message or an answer on the page, and without the inbox's acks he would be pushed toward a channel that still has one reader. The dark flag flips by the go-live ticket whose proof is N-30's ack ladder working on stable for a day.
Why a receipt record: the owner's complaint is not knowing whether he was told; the receipt is countable on the health line and shown on the card (a small phone mark) so he sees the system told him.

provider.choice: Self-hosted ntfy on the owner's cluster, deployed by the existing homelab-gitops path (the feat/ntfy-alerts branch of homelab-gitops already carries it, L10 section 3), reached from the host over the tailnet or WireGuard, with the ntfy app on the iPhone subscribed to one private topic with an access token.
provider.why: No app to build (APNs direct needs a signed app), no third party holding the owner's decisions (ntfy.sh public topics would), one HTTP POST per push, a click action that opens the page, priorities and tags, and the deployment path the owner already trusts (map-hosting-and-feel-rules: nothing new). The topic and token are config and a secret file; the topic name is never in a record.
provider.fallback: If the cluster ntfy is down (3 failed attempts), the bridge writes push.failed and N-41 shows it; a second provider (ntfy.sh with a long random topic) is a config option phone_push.fallback_url that is off by default and is the owner's call, because it would hand card titles to a third party (the upstream relay of #push-delivery hands over only a message id).

push-delivery.s: What broke (review F22, 2026-10-15): this volume named ntfy but not how a message reaches a locked iPhone; without upstream-base-url a self-hosted server's iOS delivery "can take hours" (ntfy docs, iOS instant notifications, fetched 2026-10-15), and the go-live proof assumed the phone would see it.
push-delivery.config: The ntfy server's base-url equals, byte for byte, the server URL the phone subscribes to (the tailnet URL of the ntfy service, from the owner's site file $HOME/.config/coq/site.env, phone_push.base_url); the upstream topic is derived from it, so a mismatch silently breaks instant delivery.
https://ntfy.sh, so the server forwards a poll request for each message to ntfy.sh, which wakes the iOS app through APNs; upstream-access-token only if ntfy.sh rate-limits the server.

auth-default-access deny-all; three tokens, each scoped to its topic: the bridge's publish token (write-only on the card topic), the probe's publish token (write-only on the probe topic, shared/outside-probe.xml#alerting), the phone's read token (read-only on both topics); no token can publish and read.

The phone reaches the ntfy server over Tailscale with on-demand VPN, the same path as the page (N-34); when it cannot reach it the app shows the upstream placeholder ("New message") and fetches the body when the tailnet is back.

homelab-gitops: a NetworkPolicy on the ntfy pod allowing egress only to DNS and ntfy.sh:443, ingress only from the tailnet operator and the host; carried by the ntfy app entry of the gitops repository, its own ticket.
push-delivery.privacy: Bodies (title, decide line, ticket title) stay on the host and the cluster; ntfy.sh and Apple see the message id, the SHA-256 of the topic URL, the timing and the cluster's egress IP, and the placeholder text; nothing else leaves. This is the statement the owner accepts at go-live.
push-delivery.receipts: push.receipt 200 means the provider (the cluster ntfy) accepted the message and returned its id; push.observed 200 means the owner opened it or the page drew the card after it. Delivery is at least once: a lease handover or a replayed effect may send twice, never zero times while the provider answers; there is no exactly-once claim and no recall.
push-delivery.probe: Probe alerts (shared/outside-probe.xml#alerting) use the same server and the phone's read token but their own topic and publish token; the bridge never publishes there and the probe never depends on the bridge.
push-delivery.proof: Go-live proof: a real card on stable with the iPhone locked for 30 minutes shows the notification within 10 s on Wi-Fi and again on cellular; the notification opens the page; push.receipt and push.observed exist; with ntfy.sh blocked at the pod the server still accepts (receipt) and the phone shows the message when it next opens the app. Not run.

start.text: The bridge is a goroutine set of coq.service; it subscribes at service start; nothing is typed. It ships dark (phone_push.enabled false) and goes live by its own ticket after N-30's go-live proof, with its own proof: one card on stable produces one push on the owner's phone within 10 s, the push opens the page, and the receipt is on the card.

wait.fallback: shadow mode (count, do not send); the lease expires by ttl and the next holder sends; a card whose receipt is missing after 60 s is found by the level-triggered scan (mechanism step 7) and sent then

wait.timeout: 10 s per attempt; 3 attempts at 10, 30, 90 s
wait.fallback: push.failed 500, alert on N-41; the card is already on the page, so nothing waits on the push

lists open cards without a receipt, failed record or terminal skip older than 60 s, and quiet-hours skips whose window has ended, and sends them, so a push dropped by a crash or held by quiet hours is sent later; bounded by the operation key
push.refused 400; a template fix ticket; the card is unaffected

waits.no-cog: The cog that could stall this node is the provider. Timeout: 3 attempts over 130 s. Fallback: the failed record, the alert, and the page itself, which never depended on the push. The push is a doorbell; the mail is on the page.

retries.rule: Network and 5xx errors retry 3 times with the 10, 30, 90 s ladder; 4xx never retries (a config defect); after 3 the failure is a record and an alert; the 60 s scan is the recovery after a crash; the idempotency key makes every retry safe.

many-agents-at-once.readers: Any number of seats read this volume.
many-agents-at-once.workers: Build tickets touch internal/owner/pushbridge, the phone_push section of the service config and its schema, and the gitops app entry for ntfy (a separate repository, its own ticket); nothing else.

collision.what: two service instances during an upgrade

many-agents-at-once.collision: The lease pushbridge admits one sender; the other shadows; a push sent by both anyway (lease handover race) is caught by the receipt's operation key: the second commit replays the first receipt and stops. At worst the phone gets two pushes for one card once per upgrade, which the receipt count shows and which is acceptable because the push is a doorbell.

collision.what: a card closes while the push is in flight

many-agents-at-once.collision: The push lands; the page shows the card done; no recall. The skip check before the send narrows the window to the POST's duration.

The per-tick cap in N-28 bounds the deck; the bridge adds a rate cap (phone_push.max_per_minute, default 6) and folds the rest into one summary push ("4 more cards waiting") with one receipt per folded card marked folded=true, so the phone never buzzes sixty times.

collision.what: the owner answers from the push before the receipt is written

many-agents-at-once.collision: The ruling and the receipt are independent records; order does not matter; the card's phone mark appears when the receipt lands.
many-agents-at-once.test: tests run two bridge goroutines against a fake provider under the fake clock: one receipt per card, the loser shadows, a provider 503 twice then 200 yields one receipt with attempt 3, a 401 yields push.failed with no retry, ten cards in a minute yield six pushes plus one summary.

path.what: the ntfy access token, mode 0600, written once by the owner through coq owner push-token (reads from a prompt, never from an argument that lands in shell history)

path.p: store rows push.receipt, push.observed, push.failed, push.skipped, push.refused, push.folded
path.what: in N-01; receipts for the life of the card; others 30 days
path.cleanup: registered with N-45 as store retention class owner-surface

path.p: journal of coq.service, lines prefixed push-bridge:
path.what: one line per send, failure, skip; never the topic, never the token

path.p: cluster: the ntfy deployment's cache volume
path.what: owned by the gitops app, not this node; its retention is the ntfy config (cache-duration 12h)
path.cleanup: kept by its own system: ntfy expires the cache after 12 h; removing the volume is the owner's gitops change; named here so N-45 can list it

edges.out: the push (no DAG node; the owner is the sink; his act returns through N-32)
edges.uses: the tailnet URL without the key
edges.gated-by: dark until the inbox is live

look.rule: Title: the card's about line (at most 60 chars, cut at a word). Body: the decide question, then one line "Recommended: <label>", then the ticket id and full title on its own line when there is one; every sentence 15 words or fewer; no record id, pid, pane or path; no key. Priority high for 500 and 503 causes, default otherwise. Tags: a card, a lamp, or a stop sign by cause class (ntfy emoji tags; the page itself carries the Krastorio look, the push is the phone's own notification style). Click: opens the page over the tailnet.
look.check: The fixture test renders one push per cause class and asserts the word counts, the absence of the key pattern and the presence of the full ticket title; a screenshot of a real push on the owner's phone is the go-live proof.

item.proof: test: a stable card with phone_push.enabled true yields one POST to the fake provider and one push.receipt 200 within 1 s
test: with enabled false the same card yields push.skipped dark and no POST
test: provider 503 twice then 200 yields one receipt at attempt 3; 401 yields push.failed with no retry

checklist.item: The ladder and the 4xx rule hold

item.proof: test: two bridge goroutines yield one receipt; the loser's put gets 409
test: 10 cards in a minute yield 6 pushes and one summary; 10 receipts, 4 folded
test: a push body with a key pattern or a 16-word sentence is refused 400 and not sent
ntfy app entry merged in homelab-gitops, Argo synced, topic subscribed on the phone with a token; coq owner push-token stored the token with mode 0600

checklist.item: The provider is up on the owner's path

item.proof: test: a card skipped for quiet-hours is pushed by the scan at the end of the window when still open and unseen; a card seen on the page meanwhile is not
not-run: the go-live proof of #push-delivery on a locked iPhone, Wi-Fi and cellular, within 10 s
N-30 ack ladder proof recorded before this node's enabled flag flips

permissions.runs-as: inside coq.service as the service user coq-svc (shared/authority.xml#principals); reads the publish token file; egress to the ntfy host only (the service's outbound allow-list names it)
permissions.may: subscribe to cards and the configured alert kinds; POST to the provider; write push.* records
permissions.may-not: send anything but a card or a configured alert; include the key, a record id or a path; take an answer back (the push has no reply action); run in a pod (the token stays on the host, D23)
permissions.owner-only: storing or rotating the token; enabling the fallback provider; setting quiet hours

counter.name: push_failed_total
counter.on: N-06; any increase is an alert

runbook.op: coq owner push-token (prompts; writes ${COQ_STATE}/owner/push/token with mode 0600; writes push.token.set 100 with no token in it)
coq owner push-test (sends "bearings test" to the topic; writes a receipt with card=test)
flip phone_push.enabled in the service config by the go-live ticket after N-30's proof; coq reload
phone_push.quiet (UTC window) by the owner's ruling, set by pull request; a card in the window is pushed when it ends (mechanism step 7)
read push.failed or push.skipped for the card; failed names the provider error; skipped names the reason; the page is unaffected either way
tools/bearings/bin/cleanup-push.sh --token (owner-only), cleanup-journal.sh; store retention by N-45
runbook.cost: An ntfy deployment on the cluster and an app on the phone; a token file on the host; a doubled push once per upgrade at worst.

sources.source: N-52 row: ships dark until the Go inbox is live
phone push channel added after as a bridge; source note names the ntfy branch
homelab-gitops branch feat/ntfy-alerts, the real cluster gitops repo
from the phone, while a card sat on a page he could not reach: the question comes to him where he is
V05 infrastructure failures retried, never test failures (the 4xx rule); V13 the doorbell is not the mail
no secret access for pods; the token stays on the host
15 words; ticket with full title; no artifact links
use the existing Jenkins, ghcr, gitops, Argo path; nothing new

item.what: APNs direct or a native app
item.reason: needs a signed app and an Apple developer account for a doorbell
no click-to-open with the cookie, no priority, a third party in the path
card titles would leave the owner's infrastructure; kept as an owner-enabled fallback only

item.what: a reply action in the push (answer from the notification)
item.reason: D20: the page is the one surface; an answer must be a durable POST with a receipt, not a notification tap
the phone would buzz constantly; cards and owner-acts alerts only

item.what: putting the key in the click URL
item.reason: the key in a push log is the L08 finding 11 again; the cookie from the first open suffices

item.what: going live together with the inbox
item.reason: C58 ordered it after; a push to a one-reader channel repeats the old defect
